Subject: Vendor onboarding: TIN verification & required tax residency evidence for PO activation

Hi Maria,

Thanks for submitting the initial paperwork for Lumen Dynamics — appreciate the quick turnaround. We're close to activating PO-2027-0874 but our finance team needs a couple of final tax items to complete vendor verification: 

Required (please provide at least one set below):
- Signed W-8BEN-E (PDF) showing the legal entity name and signature.
- Official IRS TIN verification letter for the vendor EIN (commonly IRS Letter 147C or CP575). This is required for payments routed from our US entity to prevent backup withholding and to confirm the EIN on file.

Additional (if original docs are not in English):
- Certified English translation of any non-English tax certificate or residency document.

Optional but helpful:
- A bank letter (on bank letterhead) confirming the account name matches the taxpayer name and the IBAN.

I attached a short guidance doc (W8-questions-attachment-guidance.pdf) that explains acceptable forms. If you don't have the IRS letter, let us know whether you can request a 147C from the IRS or provide a CP575 issued at EIN assignment.

Next steps and timeline: we need these docs by EOD Tue 9 Mar 2027 to keep the PO on schedule. If we don't have them by then, finance may place the PO in conditional hold until verification is complete.

Doc upload options: secure DocuSign transaction (link below), SFTP, or directly reply with encrypted attachments. I've included the DocuSign envelope for convenience: https://app.docusign.com/transactions/ABCD-1234-PO-2027-0874

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez

Sergio / Aditya,

Thanks for the heads-up and for the attachments from Lumen. A couple of clarifications from Finance/legal before we flip the PO to active: 

1) The W-8BEN-E received looks complete but we cannot rely on a foreign tax residency certificate alone to validate an EIN for US payment routing. For US-sourced payments we require IRS confirmation of the EIN on file (Letter 147C is standard) or a copy of CP575 issued at EIN assignment.

2) If Lumen cannot obtain a 147C/CP575 in a timely manner, we can accept a notarized SS-4 acceptance copy plus a bank letter showing the same legal name and account number; however this path requires extra review and will delay payment onboarding.

3) Please ask the vendor to provide certified English translations of the Certificate_of_Tax_Residence document. Non-English originals are fine as supplemental, but our compliance team needs an English version for the vendor file.

Operational impact: Finance will place PO-2027-0874 into conditional hold on Wed 10 Mar 2027 if requested documents are not uploaded. Once we have either (A) 147C/CP575 or (B) notarized SS-4 + bank letter + translated residency cert, we can clear the hold.

Laura, tagging you for any legal concerns about accepting alternate evidence.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Procurement & Payments | Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — looping back with next steps so we can avoid a hold.

Acceptable options (choose one and upload to the DocuSign envelope or reply with encrypted attachments):
A) IRS Letter 147C or CP575 confirming the EIN (preferred) + signed W-8BEN-E + translated Certificate of Tax Residence; OR
B) Notarized SS-4 acceptance copy showing EIN + bank letter on bank letterhead confirming account name matches legal entity + translated residency certificate (this is our backup route and will require an extra compliance review).

If you think Letter 147C will take longer than 72 hours to obtain, please elect option B and upload the notarized SS-4 + bank letter.

DocuSign (preferred upload): https://app.docusign.com/transactions/ABCD-1234-PO-2027-0874
Alternate: SFTP upload (we'll share credentials on request) or encrypted reply to this thread.

We appreciate your help — if you can confirm which option you'll provide and an ETA, we'll keep the PO in pending state until documents arrive.

Best,
Sergio
